title: Light flashes answered by a stationary light over the prairie at the November-1 launch control facility
place_text: November-1 launch control facility, Ellsworth AFB missile field, South Dakota

tellings.quote: just watching it a couple of minutes went by may maybe a minute and a half and all of a sudden this thing goes out on out on out and on and it just sent shivers up me and I went wow they do see me
I just flipped the thing off and on, off and on, off and on three times.
tellings.difference: Says he flipped the lights three times.
tellings.link_reason: The same 1977 episode at the November 1 launch control facility, where Mario flashed his lights at a light and it flashed back.

as_told.title: Mario flashes his lights at a light in the sky and it flashes back
as_told.place_text: November 1 launch control facility, Ellsworth AFB missile field, South Dakota

tellings.quote: I thought for a minute and, all of a sudden, got the idea to flash the facility lights off and on as a signal.

My SAT team partner, Sgt. -------, got curious and after I had flashed the lights six to eight times we walked outside together to look at the object. There it was, no change in its appearance or position but, a moment or two after ------- made some comment about the light, it went out!

plain: Mario Woods, an Air Force guard at a missile launch control post in South Dakota in 1977, says he saw a still light over the prairie, flashed the post's lights off and on three times, and after a minute or so the light went "out on out on out and on", which sent shivers up him: "wow they do see me." He tells it first-hand to Michels as the start of the night he says he was abducted. In the account he wrote for the researcher Robert Hastings in 2017, he flashed the lights "six to eight times", and the light "went out" "a moment or two after" his partner "made some comment about the light", then "re-appeared to the north and seemed closer"; whether that was an answer to his signal, the 2017 text neither says nor rules out.

discussion.by: Former USAF Missile Security Policeman Tells of Apparent UFO Abduction at ICBM Site
discussion.text: In the account Woods wrote for Hastings in 2017 he flashed the facility lights "six to eight times", and the light "went out" "a moment or two after" his partner "made some comment about the light", then "re-appeared to the north and seemed closer"; the later telling has three flashes answered by the light going off and on. The step from a light that went out to a light that answered the flashes is the later telling's reading; the 2017 text neither states nor excludes it.
